notes: MCP SERVER. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first: tools are `Tool` trait objects in a `ToolRegistry`, called with a `ToolContext`. Build the server that exposes a registry over MCP Streamable HTTP, as server.ts does: bind 127.0.0.1 on a random port, require the same bearer token scheme, keep per-client sessions, answer tools/list and tools/call, and write the same `mcp-endpoint.json` file (same field names and values, so scripts/mcp-call.py and bin/revb.mjs keep working unchanged) into `ToolContext::data_dir`. Use the official Rust SDK: the `rmcp` crate (version 3.9) with its streamable HTTP server transport (StreamableHttpService with LocalSessionManager, served by axum on tokio). You have no training knowledge of this exact API: read its documentation and source under ~/.cargo/registry/src after adding the dependency (run `cargo fetch` or a build), and write a ServerHandler by hand with list_tools and call_tool backed by the registry (do not use the #[tool] macros: tools are registered at run time). Public API: `pub fn start(registry: Arc<ToolRegistry>, context: Arc<ToolContext>) -> Result<McpServer, String>` that starts its own tokio runtime on a background thread and returns the URL and the Authorization header value, plus a way to stop it. Port the behaviors server.ts wraps around tool calls: the X-Rever-Catalog header modes and tool-profile filtering (the profile rules are already ported in the rever-tool-profile crate, use it as a path dependency), result paging (tools/paging.ts with the ResultStore in rever-tools-api utils), and the per-result notes about dialogs and downloads where the data is available (take them from a trait or closure the app can supply later; default none). tool-profile-state.ts persists the active profile under Electron's userData: use `ToolContext::data_dir` with the same file name and JSON shape. The tools in tool_profile.ts and paging.ts are registered by this crate: `ToolDef::new("<name>", ...)` with the name as a string literal, description verbatim, input schema converted from zod to JSON Schema. Verification: integration tests that start the server with a registry of fake tools and act as a client over real HTTP (reqwest or the rmcp client): initialize, tools/list, tools/call, wrong token rejected, endpoint file contents; and run `python3 scripts/mcp-call.py --list` against a server started from a test or example binary of this crate (the script reads mcp-endpoint.json from REVER_USER_DATA_DIR) and report what it printed. serde_json's preserve_order feature is enabled in this crate: keep it.
